## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition requires immediate professional attention. All other measured components are in good condition.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet |

The tank is holding fluid at the outlet level. Solids content is within the normal range and does not require pumping at this time.

## PUMP OPERATION
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

The pump motor is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic resistance -- that is, no fluid is being moved. The motor is at risk of overheating without the cooling effect of fluid circulation.

**Probable causes:** broken or missing impeller, severed or disconnected discharge line, or dry-running condition.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENTS
| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | No structural defects observed |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated; light soiling |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and operating |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry, no breakout or ponding |

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL -- Immediate Professional Attention Required**

The effluent pump is operating at no load (22.2% FLA). A qualified technician must immediately examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or blockage, and check the pump impeller for damage or absence. Do not delay this assessment. Continued operation without hydraulic load will damage the motor.

**Secondary Actions (after pump is restored to normal operation)**

- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is confirmed normal.
- Recommend measuring dissolved oxygen at the next maintenance visit to establish a treatment baseline for this aerobic system.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Operation and Your System
Your system uses an effluent pump to move treated water from the tank to the dispersal field. The pump is running, but it is not moving water. This is a serious condition that must be corrected before the system can function. Do not attempt to troubleshoot the pump yourself. Contact a qualified technician immediately.

### Solids Management
This maintenance visit recorded solids at approximately 23 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable.
